full_judgment:
Mr. Quazi Reza-U1 Hoque, J :- The instant Civil Revision, Rule was issued on 24.08.2010 calling upon the opposite parties to show as to why the judgment and decree dated 24.06.2010 complained of in the petition moved in Court today should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The petitioners have preferred this Civil Revision against the judgment and decree dated 24.06.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Appeal No.10 of 2007 reversing the judgment and decree dated 20.11.2006 and 27.11.2006 respectively, passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd  Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.68 of 2006 dismissed the suit by ex-parte judgment. 

 4. The facts, in short, as has been in the petition is that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed a title suit before the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur for declaration of title in the land, measuring 1.122 acres out of 1.74 acres of total land alleging inter alia that the original owner of the suit land was Baldha Court of Wards Estate. The C.S. record was prepared correctly in the name of the Manager, Baldha Court of Wards Estate. Thereafter the Government of East Pakistan acquired the land by State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. After Liberation of Bangladesh the land was taken over by the Government of Bangladesh. The predecessor of the plaintiffs, Salim Uddin acquired title in the suit Plot No.6 1 I by the way of lease from the Government and the lease deed was registered vide Deed No.310 dated 09.11.1975. After 15 years the lease became permanent settlement on the basis of the terms of the said deed. After the death of Salim Uddin the plaintiffs are owner of the land by inheritance. The defendant claimed the suit land through R.S. Record in the name of Sabdul Munsi and hence and the case. 

 6. The learned trial Court Judge examined only one P.W. on behalf of the plaintiffs and the learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs have not succeeded to prove that in the disputed R.S. Khatian No.295 is the land of that Plot No.611. In the impugned judgment it was also found that the plaintiff has failed to prove ownership and title over the suit Plot No.2333. 

 9. The learned Appellate Court below perused the documents and evidence on records and the Advocate Commissioner Report and the appeal was allowed on merit. 

 10. The Appellate Court below allowed the appeal only on the basis of the Advocate Commissioner Report and, as such, committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice. 

 11. Mr. Sikder Mahmudur Razi with Mr. Wayesh Al-Haroni, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondent-petitioners submitted that the learned Court below without applying his judicial mind allowed the appeal and the appellate Court below committed error of law resulting in the decision occasion failure of justice. 

 12. Mr. S. N. Goswami with Ms. Afsana Begum, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties by simple submission submitted that in the appellate Court the Advocate Commissioner's Report clearly reflected by deposition of filed book, sketch map that C.S. Plot No.611 as R.S. Plot No.2333 in the R.S. Record, and therefore the error and ambiguity caused by the learned Assistant Judge in the trial Court has been rectified. So, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 13. On perusal of the submissions made by the learned Advocates for both the parties, the impugned judgment, the judgment of the trial Court and the L.C. Record, it is quite apparent that the crux of the trial Court judgment is that – 

 14. On perusal of the Advocate Commissioner's Report, it became absolutely clear that the C.S. Plot No.611 was converted to and renumbered as R.S. Plot No.2333. So, the ambiguity with regard to possession of the plaintiff-appellant-opposite parties became crystal clear, and as such, the learned Judge of the appellate Court rightly verdicted the suit on appeal, and therefore it deserves no interference. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree passed the learned Joint District Judge, 1M Court, Gazipur, on 24.06.2010 and 30.06.2010 respectively in Title Appeal No.10 of 2007 is hereby maintained. 

 18. Send down the L.C.R. with a copy of the judgment and order to the concerned Court below immediately.
